title: After-Hours Pocketbook: On-call Handoff & Temporary Procedures
content:
Purpose: quick, scannable pocket guide for late shifts — handoff bullets, temporary workarounds, and what I think matters right now. NOT the canonical runbook; put fixes into Confluence and PRs when stable.

TL;DR (first 2 minutes):
- Check PagerDuty: any active incidents? Note customer impact tag (prod/pp/prod-dedicated).
- Dashboard glance: p50/p95 token latency, GPU mem pressure, total queued requests. If red, jump to "Immediate triage".
- Look for recurring alerts from the last 6h (same signature). Likely a queued-backlog issue.

Handoff template (what to tell next shift):
- 3-line summary: "Healthy, but increased OOMs on dedicated-gpu-pool B after 21:00 UTC; mitigated with force-scale to burst-1. See incident notes INC-4123."
- What I did: scaled pool B + temp limited model variant to quantized-v2 to reduce memory.
- Open follow-ups: reproduce at lower seq len, add cache warm-up for heavy-user tenant X.
- Where I left things: autoscaler set to manual burst for 2h, reverted at 02:00 if stable.
- Suggested priority: high — investigate memory fragmentation and kernel selection under qkv-fused.

Immediate triage checklist (if latency/throughput alert):
1) Confirm conditions: check /console/metrics -> route /v1/generate latency spike.
2) Check serving-runtime logs (prod-gpu-*/pods): grep for "alloc failed" or "KV cache miss storm".
3) If OOMs showing across pods, mark as capacity issue and scale pool. Command: 
   kubectl -n redwood scale --replicas=6 deployment/dedicated-gpu-pool-b
   (quick note: we prefer autoscaler but during incidents manual scale avoids churn)
4) If only one pod failing: collect pod logs, restart pod: 
   kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/dedicated-gpu-pool-b --selector=pod-name=<pod>
5) If route-specific, flip route to fallback model (route override):
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://api.redwood.ai/admin/routes/override -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"gptx-8k-quant"}'

Temporary workarounds I've used (notes & gotchas):
- Quick memory pressure mitigation: switch heavy-tenant routes to quantized model variant. Pros: immediate lower mem. Cons: slight quality regression and unknown perf on long-lm sequences.
- Avoid restarting the entire daemonset unless multiple pods show kernel OOMs — restarts purge KV caches and spike tail latency.
- If we see "kv cache corrupt" warnings, do NOT rehydrate caches immediately; follow seq: cordon -> restart -> let pool accept low-traffic rehydration.

Common signals and how I interpret them quickly:
- Sustained p95 token latency > 2.5s and queue length > 50: batching saturation -> increase batch size or scale horizontally.
- Frequent "deadline exceeded" in API logs but healthy GPU util: probable network or proxy timeouts (check envoy).
- OOM + sudden drop in throughput: look at model variant, quantization mismatch, or CUDA driver noise.

Useful commands (copy-paste safe):
- Get recent incidents: pd-summaries --since 6h --service oncall || echo 'no PD incidents'
- Pod OOM logs: kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=serving-runtime --since=2h | grep -i oom
- Check GC/fragmentation: ssh perf-host-02 "nvidia-smi -q | grep -A5 'FB Memory Usage'"
- Scale pool (manual): ./infra/tools/pool-scale --pool dedicated-gpu-pool-b --replicas 6 --reason "night: temp mitigation"

Escalation matrix (who to call if P1):
- On-call infra lead: Marco Alvarez (pager)
- Serving runtime owner: Janelle Park (slack @janelle)
- SRE manager (if >30m outage): Priya Menon (phone)
- Legal/CS: for customer-impacting incidents call Samir Patel (CS lead) — customer comms template: see linked Confluence page.

Recent incident notes (short):
- 2026-03-09 21:40 UTC: memory spike on pool B after a big batched rerank from tenant X. Root suspect: large seq lengths + dynamic batching that ignored max_seq parameter. Mitigation: applied route override to cap seq to 2048 and limited batch size in config. See JIRA-INC-4123 for timeline.

Open TODOs I want to hand off:
- Add a quick telemetry panel for "batch size distribution by tenant" (helps spot bad clients).
- Add preflight check gating for large rerank jobs in hosted API (prevent unthrottled large-seq requests).
- Formalize temp fallback model behavior in product console (so SREs don't have to curl admin endpoints).

Notes to self (things I scribbled during the shift):
- Patch in serving-runtime PR 789 seems to reduce fragmentation; run e2e perf next low-traffic window.
- Remember to clear manual burst override at 02:00 if no new incidents.
- If PD keeps flaring with same signature, escalate to research: maybe kernel selection bug.

Slack snippets for handoff (pasteable):
- "Handoff from Rina: Increased OOMs earlier 21:30 UTC on dedicated-gpu-pool-B, temporary scale+quantized fallback applied. Autoscaler set to manual for now. Check INC-4123 and pool metrics; I left a follow-up list in Drive."

Open questions / unknowns (to investigate later):
- Why did dynamic batching ignore configured max_seq for tenant X? (config vs. SDK bug?)
- Any correlation between driver version 525.x and increased fragmentation in qkv-fused kernels?

End notes: this is messy by design — it's a pocketbook for waking up, triaging fast, and leaving a clear trail. If you find a repeatable fix, please convert the workaround into a Confluence runbook and tag me.

Last checked signals at 03:09 UTC: p50=0.09s, p95=1.4s, queued=12, GPU util=74%, OOMs last 6h=3.

-- Rina K. (late shift), 2026-03-11
